The layout fails to escape characters forbidden by the XML 1.0 standard, producing malformed XML output that conforming XML parsers must reject with a fatal error, potentially causing downstream log processing systems to silently drop or fail to index affected log records. Affected versions are 2.7 through 2.25.3 and 3.0.0-alpha1 through 3.0.0-beta2. It carries a CVSS v3.1 score of 7.5 (High) and a CVSS v4.0 score of 6.9 (Medium) (Github Advisory, oss-security). Technical details The root cause is CWE-116 (Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output): the Log4j1XmlLayout class in the Log4j 1-to-Log4j 2 bridge does not sanitize log event data before embedding it in XML output, allowing control characters and other code points forbidden by the XML 1.0 standard to pass through unescaped. Two configurations are affected: (1) direct use of Log4j1XmlLayout in a Log4j Core 2 configuration file, and (2) use of the Log4j 1 compatibility layer with org.apache.log4j.xml.XMLLayout as the layout class. An unauthenticated network attacker can trigger the issue by sending crafted input containing XML-forbidden characters to any application endpoint that logs user-controlled data, causing the resulting XML log record to be malformed. The fix, merged in PR #4078, sanitizes output by replacing invalid XML 1.0 code points with the Unicode replacement character U+FFFD (Github PR, Github Advisory). Impact Successful exploitation causes downstream log processing systems (e.g., SIEM platforms, log indexers, compliance monitoring tools) to reject or silently drop affected log records due to malformed XML, resulting in a high integrity impact on log data pipelines. There is no confidentiality or direct availability impact on the vulnerable application itself; the primary consequence is loss of log visibility, which can undermine security monitoring, incident response, and regulatory compliance.
